dedupe_keys.name: cpssm compact phase screen gnss scintillation simulator

description: The Compact Phase-screen-based Scintillation Model (CPSSM) is a MATLAB tool that simulates ionospheric scintillation, the rapid fluctuations in amplitude and phase of GNSS signals caused by irregularities in the ionosphere, so that receivers and algorithms can be tested against weak and strong scintillation. It models the ionosphere as a thin turbulent phase screen and lets users set receiver position and velocity, simulation time and ionospheric conditions for GPS and Galileo satellites, downloading RINEX ephemerides automatically, and it outputs time series of amplitude and phase, detrended phase and normalised power spectral densities. It covers any receiver location and time for which ephemerides are available. The original GPS scintillation simulator was created by the CU SENSE Lab at the University of Colorado Boulder (copyright 2020, MIT-style licence), and Rubem Vasconcelos Pacelli and Rodrigo de Lima Florindo of the ITA GPS/GNSS Laboratory published a refactored and enhanced version (started December 2024, cited as of July 2025) under the MIT licence; both include third-party code under BSD and other notices, such as an IGRF implementation and a Wavelab subset. It is free on GitHub but needs a MATLAB licence to run. Caveats: the phase-screen model is a simplification of real ionospheric structure and the refactored version supports GPS and Galileo only. It supports hazard exposure and resilience testing of satellite positioning services and the receivers that other infrastructures rely on; a related record is the FARR ionospheric radio propagation code.
